run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T17:56:11Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is caused by failing checkout requests. Every frontend span carrying STATUS_CODE_ERROR belongs to the checkout path (POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder); all other frontend operations show zero errors, and roughly 81% of POST /api/checkout attempts now fail (0.4148/s ERROR vs 0.0963/s UNSET at 18:05:11), with errors appearing from about 17:55-17:56 onward. Every failing span's duration is in the 5-10 s bucket both at the frontend and at checkout, so the requests are hanging, not being rejected quickly. Inside checkout the only slow (>5 s) child operation is its HTTP POST client span (0.4185/s of 0.7074/s); ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, CartService/GetCart, CurrencyService/Convert, PaymentService/Charge and orders publish remain under 5 s. That HTTP POST is the shipping quote call: shipping's /get-quote server spans and its POST quote client spans both take 5-10 s and are marked STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.4185/s, while the quote service's own span rate collapses from about 0.4/s before 17:56 to 0.03-0.08/s through the incident, and the requests it does handle complete in about 2 ms (all quote spans are <=2 ms). Both quote pods are Ready, have never restarted, run the same image since 17:20, use ~0.0005 CPU cores, emit no error logs, and each serves only a trickle (28 and 21 log lines in the 17:56:11-18:06:11 window), in one-minute-aligned bursts around second :08. The failure is therefore localized to the shipping -> quote hop: quote's application is demonstrably healthy and idle, and most quote calls never reach it. The exact mechanism at that hop (dropped/undelivered traffic, datapath backend programming, or a stall in the pod's pre-application accept path) is not resolvable with the available evidence, so the conclusion is partial and no single Kubernetes object can be named as the origin without over-reach.

The frontend error rate by span_name is zero for every non-checkout operation for the whole 16:56:11-18:11:59 window, and the checkout-path series (POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) first becomes non-zero at the 17:57:11 sample (0.1963/s) after being 0 at 17:55:11.

Shipping is the slow dependency of checkout: at 18:05:11 shipping /get-quote has 0.5148/s total but only 0.0963/s <=5000 ms, and its POST quote client span likewise has 0.5148/s total with only 0.0963/s <=5000 ms, so 0.4185/s of both hang beyond 5 s; by contrast the quote service's spans total 0.0963/s for POST /getquote, calculate-quote and {closure}, all <=5000 ms.

Frontend error spans at 18:05:11 are grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.4148/s, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 0.4148/s, POST 0.4148/s and POST /api/checkout 0.4148/s; all other frontend operations (including cart, ad, data routes and tcp.connect) are 0.

Traffic to the quote service collapses during the incident while requests keep arriving at shipping: quote POST /getquote falls from about 0.38-0.53/s at the samples up to 17:56:11 to 0.03-0.08/s from 17:56:11 through 18:06:11, whereas shipping /get-quote stays at 0.36-0.47/s over the same samples.
The requests the quote service does handle are fast: at 18:05:11 its total span rate is 0.2889/s and 0.2815/s is <=2 ms (all buckets above 2 ms equal 0.2889/s), so no quote span is slow.

Both quote pods keep serving only a trickle during the incident: quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b logged 28 'Calculated quote' lines and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt logged 21 in the 17:56:11-18:06:11 window, against a pre-incident quote span rate of roughly 0.4 requests/s.

shipping's logs show repeated 'Requesting quote' lines without the following 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' completion after about 17:59:15 (e.g. 17:59:15.92, 17:59:16.47, 17:59:21.93, 17:59:25.60, 17:59:29.96 ... 17:59:58.92), while the two that did complete at 17:59:12-13 logged the full sequence.

The slowness is confined to the checkout chain at 18:05:11: spans over 1 s exist only for frontend (1.9074/s), frontend-proxy (1.1852/s), checkout (1.3778/s) and shipping (0.9185/s); cart, currency, payment, product-catalog, email, ad, image-provider and quote all have 0.

checkout keeps receiving the same order volume throughout: its oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span rate stays between 0.3555/s and 0.5333/s from 16:54 through 18:05 and is 0.4851/s at the 18:04:11 sample, so the incident is hanging requests, not reduced traffic.

The quote workload is unchanged and healthy by its own object state: quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt were created 2026-11-16T17:20:01Z with restartCount 0, no lastState.terminated, the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-quote (digest sha256:f44773a5...), and their ReplicaSet quote-6b5877698d reports 2/2 ready; shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 is 1/1 ready with 0 restarts.

The quote Service is populated: its Endpoints object lists both pod addresses (100.96.2.155 nodeName i-0f88eaa39b314c60b targetRef quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt, and 100.96.4.53 nodeName i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e targetRef quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b) on port 8080, and the shipping Service lists 100.96.4.227 (shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9).
No pod in otel-demo restarted or was replaced around the incident: all 22 pods were created 2026-11-16T17:20:01Z-17:22:01Z, all show restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated reason or exit code.

All five nodes (i-04f5a8f1af169d973, i-057763a5797b8b461, i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, i-0c466d0294b17ee91, i-0f88eaa39b314c60b) report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False (CiliumIsUp), so there is no node-level pressure signal during the incident window's end state.

Container CPU shows the quote pods idle and unthrottled during the incident: at 18:05:11 container_cpu_usage_seconds_total rates are 0.00058 cores (quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt) and 0.00052 cores (quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b) versus 0.00180 cores for shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9.

Cluster DNS and networking pods are stable: both coredns-b5494cbf4 pods have restartCount 0 and have been running since 2026-11-12T02:21, and the cilium agents (including cilium-jz8gx on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, the node hosting shipping and frontend) all report Running with 0 restarts.

Before the incident the same chain was fast: the checkout spans returned by Jaeger for 17:40:05-17:40:17 include checkout HTTP POST children of 65.9 ms, 17.3 ms and 5.4 ms and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder server spans of 255.9 ms, 198.0 ms and 150.8 ms with status tag rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

The quote application itself shows no fault signal of its own: every span it produced during the incident is <=2 ms, its pods are 2/2 ready with 0 restarts and no terminated state, and its CPU usage is about 0.0005 cores, so 'quote is slow or overloaded' is not supported; only the arrival of requests is degraded.

Not all frontend latency is new: at the 17:40:11 baseline, frontend already had 0.2630/s and frontend-proxy 0.3778/s of spans over 1 s (checkout 0.0222/s, shipping 0), so the pre-existing slow-span background must not be attributed to this incident; what is new is the checkout/shipping slow population (1.3778/s and 0.9185/s at 18:05:11) plus the error status.

Rejected: a rollout, restart, eviction or OOM explains the change. All otel-demo pods (including both quote pods and shipping) predate the incident (created 17:20-17:22), have restartCount 0, no lastState.terminated reason/exit code, quote's ReplicaSet is 2/2 ready and the image digest is unchanged, and the otel-demo Warning-event query returned no items.

Rejected: the frontend is the origin of the errors. Every frontend error span is a checkout-path span, all other frontend operations show zero errors, and the frontend's cart/ad/product/recommendation calls keep succeeding; the frontend is reporting a failure produced by its checkout dependency.

Rejected: the checkout service is the origin. Checkout's other dependencies are fast during the incident (ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, CartService/GetCart, CurrencyService/Convert, PaymentService/Charge, orders publish all <=5 s, and at 200 ms GetCart 0.5148/0.5148 and Convert 1.0074/1.0074), and the only slow checkout child is the HTTP POST shipping-quote call; checkout's slowness is fully accounted for by waiting on shipping.

Rejected: a node-level failure explains it. All five nodes are Ready with no memory/disk/PID pressure and NetworkUnavailable False, and services co-located with shipping on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e (frontend, product-catalog, cart, payment, currency) keep serving without errors or slow spans.

Primary hypothesis: most requests from shipping to the quote Service are not being delivered to the quote application. Shipping calls /get-quote at 0.5148/s and its POST quote client spans hang 5-10 s and end in STATUS_CODE_ERROR, but quote's application handles only 0.0963/s (5-10 per minute in pod logs) and is idle; the undelivered calls time out at the client rather than being answered by quote.

Secondary hypothesis for the mechanism: the delivery gate is periodic. Both quote pods (on different nodes, i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e and i-0f88eaa39b314c60b) accept requests only in short bursts aligned to about second :08 of each minute, which points to a shared 60-second-cadence state - for example Service/datapath backend programming or connection-state refresh for the quote VIP (100.70.135.204) - rather than random packet loss; this cannot be confirmed without dataplane visibility.

Alternative hypothesis that the available data cannot exclude: the quote pods' pre-application accept path (listen backlog saturation or a fronting web-server/worker stall inside the container) is what blocks requests, since such a stall would also leave the application idle with no spans and no logs for the unaccepted requests; it is not distinguishable from a network delivery failure with the tools available here.

Capture the failing hop directly: run a TCP-level capture (or hubble observe) on shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and both quote pods for destination port 8080 while reproducing, to see whether SYNs to the quote Service VIP reach the pods and whether handshakes complete or time out.

Check the dataplane/policy layer for the quote Service: list EndpointSlices and any Cilium CRD policies for otel-demo (the built-in NetworkPolicy list for the namespace is empty, but the cilium-agent logs were unreadable so CRD policy and datapath program state are unverified), and confirm the Service VIP 100.70.135.204 -> endpoints 100.96.2.155:8080 / 100.96.4.53:8080 mapping is continuously programmed.

Inspect the quote container internals for a pre-application accept/queue stall (listen backlog drops, any in-container web server or worker-pool error log, pending-connection counts) and add a timeout/error log to shipping's quote HTTP client so the next occurrence records the actual failure reason instead of only an ERROR span.

gaps: Trace-level error details are unavailable for the incident: Jaeger returned no frontend traces for 17:45:00-18:11:59 and the newest trace data returned for checkout/frontend spans was 17:40:17, so the actual error message/status (e.g. whether the failing PlaceOrder/quote calls ended as deadline exceeded or connection errors) was never observed; the 5-10 s duration only suggests a client-side timeout.

The exact mechanism inside the shipping -> quote hop is unresolved: whether packets/connections are dropped before reaching the pods or the pods fail to accept them cannot be separated with the available metrics, logs and object state.

The cilium-agent containers on the shipping/quote nodes returned 0 log lines for 17:56:11-18:06:00, so dataplane drop/policy verdicts are unknown; the otel-demo NetworkPolicy list returned no objects, but Cilium CRD policies could not be queried or enumerated (the CRD list exceeded the tool's size limit).

No Warning events were returned for otel-demo or kube-system, and events that expired (including any around the ~17:55 onset) are not retrievable, so the change that started the incident is unverified. change_history is not integrated in this Run.

The frontend pod (frontend-675fd7b5c5-d2vwq) produced no log lines at all in the queried windows (lines_read 0), so frontend-side error text could not be read; shipping's error/deadline-filtered log query also returned no lines, which does not prove absence but leaves its HTTP client error detail unknown.

EndpointSlice content/history and ReplicaSet change history before the incident are not available, so it is unknown whether the quote Service's backend set changed at onset; the Endpoints object was only observed at query time (18:13), after the incident window.

No per-pod request counters exist in the available metrics (quote spans carry only service_name), so the per-pod share of the failing traffic could not be measured precisely; only pod log line counts were compared.
next_steps: Have a human with dataplane access run hubble/tcpdump between shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and the quote endpoints (100.96.2.155, 100.96.4.53, VIP 100.70.135.204:8080) during a recurrence to confirm whether connections are dropped or accepted-but-stalled.

Enumerate EndpointSlices and Cilium (CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumEndpoint) state for the quote Service, and watch Endpoints/EndpointSlice for minute-cadence churn that would match the observed :08-aligned bursts.
Inspect the quote container for a fronting web server/worker pool (accept queue drops, queue depth, error log) to confirm or exclude the pre-application stall hypothesis.

Add explicit timeout/error logging to shipping's quote HTTP client and raise the frontend/checkout client deadline visibility so the next failure records the concrete error code rather than only a 5-10 s ERROR span.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: a rollout, restart, eviction or OOM explains the change. All otel-demo pods (including both quote pods and shipping) predate the incident (created 17:20-17:22), have restartCount 0, no lastState.terminated reason/exit code, quote's ReplicaSet is 2/2 ready and the image digest is unchanged, and the otel-demo Warning-event query returned no items.

Rejected: the frontend is the origin of the errors. Every frontend error span is a checkout-path span, all other frontend operations show zero errors, and the frontend's cart/ad/product/recommendation calls keep succeeding; the frontend is reporting a failure produced by its checkout dependency.

Rejected: the checkout service is the origin. Checkout's other dependencies are fast during the incident (ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, CartService/GetCart, CurrencyService/Convert, PaymentService/Charge, orders publish all <=5 s, and at 200 ms GetCart 0.5148/0.5148 and Convert 1.0074/1.0074), and the only slow checkout child is the HTTP POST shipping-quote call; checkout's slowness is fully accounted for by waiting on shipping.

Rejected: a node-level failure explains it. All five nodes are Ready with no memory/disk/PID pressure and NetworkUnavailable False, and services co-located with shipping on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e (frontend, product-catalog, cart, payment, currency) keep serving without errors or slow spans.
